dominant_strengths: Clear triage hierarchy via Critical/Important/Routine grouping with count chips and red left-bar accents that earn attention
Strong typographic rhythm: bold 'Today' anchor, muted section labels, and consistent meta-row treatment with icons and tags
Restrained palette where red, amber, blue chips map cleanly to severity, supported by a calm cream canvas
dominant_weaknesses: Banner, progress bar, and critical block stack three competing red/green status signals in 200px, creating early visual noise
Tag styling is generic pill-on-grey; little distinction between category, time, and severity tags weakens scanability
Layout is conventional checklist UI — nothing structurally novel beyond grouping, so distinctiveness stays mid-tier
fix_priorities: Consolidate the red alert banner and the Critical section — they duplicate the same '2 tasks' message
Differentiate tag types (time vs label vs severity) via shape, weight, or icon-only treatments
Introduce subtle motion/interaction affordances (hover, swipe hints) to elevate the static feel
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral utility leads with strong triage and progress feedback; visceral polish is solid but reflective payoff is modest because the metaphor stays a familiar checklist.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — it reads as a meaningfully 'improved' task list with prioritization, progress, and urgency cues layered onto a clean baseline.
